newsitem.title: LEBANON: Profiles of Japanese Red Army guerrillas in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Profiles of Japanese Red Army guerrillas in Lebanon.

text.p: Here are brief profiles of five Japanese Red Army guerrillas sentenced to jail on Thursday by a Beirut court for offences related to their illegal stay in Lebanon.
Japanese police have released records of their past suspected activities. All are on the international wanted list on various charges.

- Kozo Okamoto, 50. With two comrades, Okamoto attacked Lod airport in Tel Aviv with grenades and machineguns. In the joint Japanese Red Army-PFLP (Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine) operation, 26 people were killed including his comrades, and 78 were wounded. He was captured and sentenced to life in prison, but was released in a Palestinian-Israeli prisoner swap in May 1985.

- Masao Adachi, 58. Adachi is the longest-serving Red Army member and acted as top spokesman for the group. When a Red Army member led four PFLP guerrillas in hijacking a Japan Air Lines plane over the Netherlands in July 1973, he was in Paris and issued a statement on the case.
- Mariko Yamamoto, 57. Yamamoto acted as liaison officer between the Japanese Red Army and Palestinian guerrilla groups. After being expelled from France in August 1974, she moved to Lebanon.

- Kazuo Tohira, 44. He was arrested in March 1975 in Sweden on suspicion of using a forged passport, and then deported to Japan. He was released several months later from a Japanese jail in exchange for the release of hostages held by Japanese Red Army members at the U.S. Embassy in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

- Haruo Wako, 49. Wako became the head of the Red Army commandos after undergoing guerrilla training in Beirut. He is suspected of involvement in the 1974 seizure of the French Embassy in The Hague, the Netherlands.
